title.value: Tackling hypo and hyper sensory processing heterogeneity in autism: From clinical stratification to genetic pathways
title.justification: The paper explicitly addresses the heterogeneity in sensory processing within autism and discusses clinical stratification and genetic pathways, as indicated in the title.
title.quote: Tackling hypo and hyper sensory processing heterogeneity in autism: From clinical stratification to genetic pathways

extractions.description: The paper explores the heterogeneity in sensory processing among autistic individuals, specifically focusing on hypo- and hyper-sensitivities. It investigates the association between sensory profiles and genetic alterations in GABAergic and glutamatergic pathways using a differential Short Sensory Profile (dSSP). The study analyzes data from autistic individuals, their relatives, and controls, and examines the genetic underpinnings of sensory differences in autism spectrum disorder.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on sensory processing in autism and the underlying genetic factors, rather than on climate or ecological sustainable development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: As an integral part of autism spectrum symptoms, sensory processing issues including both hypo and hyper sensory sensitivities.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not focus on climate or ecological sustainable development themes. Its main subject is autism spectrum disorder and related sensory processing and genetic studies.
primary_category.quote: We aimed to construct a summarizing score as a normalized and centralized ratio of the hypo- to hyper- sensitivity derived from the Short Sensory Profile (SSP), a commonly used questionnaire to explore the sensory symptoms frequently reported in autistic individuals.

secondary_categories.justification: The study does not address any secondary themes related to climate or ecological sustainable development.
secondary_categories.quote: We first asked four senior clinical experts in the field of autism spectrum (AL, AB, AM, FA) and blind to the hypothesis of this study to determine which items of the scale were dedicated to the exploration of hyper-, hypo- sensitivity or which seemed to be related to both hyper- and hypo- sensitivity.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not align with any sub-categories related to climate or ecological sustainable development.
primary_sub_category.quote: To explore the hypo/hyper-sensory profile among autistic individuals and its link with genetic alterations in GABA-ergic and glutamatergic pathways.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: There are no additional sub-category themes that relate to climate or ecological sustainable development.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: These sensory specificities may result from an excitation/inhibition imbalance with a poorly understood of their level of convergence with genetic alterations in GABA-ergic and glutamatergic pathways.

applications.justification: The paper does not discuss applications within the context of climate or ecological sustainable development.
applications.quote: A significant positive regression equation was found (F=1.7, R^{2}=0.05, p=0.001)

new_primary_category.justification: Since the content is not related to climate or ecological sustainable development, no new primary category is suggested.
new_primary_category.quote: The major limitation was the dSSP difficulty to discriminate subjects with a similar quantum of hypo- and hyper-sensory symptoms to those with no such symptoms, resulting both in a similar ratio score of 0.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: There is no evident need to suggest a new sub-category as the paper does not focus on sustainable development.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Further studies could help to better validate this scoring as an assessment tool for sensory processing anomalies.
